# Squashage

> Squashage is the graph reconstitution pipeline. Feed it classified JSON records; it squashes them into deterministic RDF graphs you can serve as Turtle, TriG, N-Triples, N-Quads, or JSON-LD. Same JSON in, same graph out — byte-identical across runs and machines, no random seeds, no network calls after startup.

Squashage is a TypeScript pipeline for converting structured JSON records into deterministic RDF graphs. It classifies each record through a cascade of configurable engines (structural, schema, SHACL-shape, URL-pattern, property-fingerprint, winkNLP, ontology, rules, conflict resolver, taxonomic narrowing), normalises the results to RDF/JS quads, and serialises the entire dataset to a single file. Output formats: Turtle, TriG, N-Triples, N-Quads, JSON-LD. The pipeline is fully deterministic: no `Math.random`, no `Date.now`, no network after startup.

## Getting started

- [Squashage home](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/): project overview, quick install, and where to look next.
- [Getting started](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/getting-started): install from source (not yet on npm), run the AONPRD demo, and open the cytoscape visualisation in a browser.
- [Walk-through](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/walk-through): end-to-end example from raw Pathfinder JSON to interactive RDF graph — config, plugin, JSON-LD output, cytoscape render.

## Usage

- [Configuration](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/configuration): the JSON config schema — top-level shape, target blocks, plugin namespaces, schema paths, output block. Source of truth: `src/schemas/squashage-config.schema.json`.
- [Pipeline](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/pipeline): ordered async middleware queue; each task receives `(next, state)` and calls `next()` to hand off. Per-record and lifecycle hooks.
- [Classifier cascade](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/classifier-cascade): eleven task classes opt-in via `pipeline:` config array. Purely deterministic — same config plus same record produces byte-identical proposals every run.
- [SHACL-shape classifier](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/shacl-shape-classifier): validates each record's projected ABox against SHACL NodeShapes and emits one proposal per conforming shape. Sits at priority 45 between schema (30) and ontology (50).
- [URL-pattern classifier](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/url-pattern-classifier): evaluates pre-compiled regular expressions against each record's URL field. Strongest signal for scraped data with consistent URL patterns.
- [Property-fingerprint classifier](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/property-fingerprint-classifier): Jaccard similarity between a record's property key set and pre-loaded class fingerprints. Catches the long tail of records lacking a clean discriminator field.
- [winkNLP entities classifier](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/winknlp-entities): deterministic, pattern-based NER over prose fields (`description`, `summary`, `rules_text`). Recovers type signal buried in human-readable text.
- [Entity-link enrichment](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/entity-link): densifies the graph by scanning prose fields after classification and inserting object-property links between records that mention each other. ~10x edge density on AONPRD-scale corpora.
- [Taxonomic narrowing](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/taxonomic-narrowing): collapses supertype proposals when a more-specific subtype is present, using the OWL `subClassOf` transitive closure from the configured TBox. Runs before the conflict resolver.
- [Ontology (json-tology)](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/ontology): two modes — hand-map (flat class → IRI map) and json-tology engine (derives SHACL shapes, JSON Schemas, and OWL TBox from a single ontology definition file).
- [Output](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/output): one file per target. Formats: Turtle, TriG, N-Triples, N-Quads, JSON-LD. Atomic write by default; stream mode available for very large datasets.
- [Provenance (PROV-O sidecar)](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/provenance): writes PROV-O classification metadata into a dedicated named graph alongside the ABox. SPARQL-queryable provenance without log scraping.
- [Viz](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/viz): `squashage viz --in graph.jsonld --out graph.html` produces a self-contained cytoscape HTML document — no network, no `node_modules` required to open.
- [Plugins](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/plugins): a plugin calls `TaskRegistry.register` or `TaskRegistry.registerHook` at module load time. Config lists plugin paths (globs, absolute, or relative). Load failure exits code 2 before any record is processed.
- [Taxonomy (upper ontology)](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/usage/taxonomy): upper ontology wiring — how the TBox is loaded, how subClassOf closure is computed, and how the narrowing pass consumes it.

## Reference

- [Architecture](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/architecture): pipeline phases, package boundaries, output contract. JSON record → classify → normalize → RDF/JS quads → serialized file.
- [Roadmap](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/roadmap): shipped features, planned work, and the v2.0 ground-up rewrite history from PathRipper.

## Demo

- [Pathfinder/AONPRD graph](https://studnicky.github.io/Squashage/examples/aonprd): interactive cytoscape graph of 12,553+ Pathfinder Second Edition records. Nodes coloured by RDF class; edges show object-property links.
